correctness.rationale: First-reset distribution has defective masses f_k with total 1−p; independently restarted waits give a geometric number K of finite waits before escape, so L=sum_{j≤K} X_j<∞ a.s. and E[z^L]=pΣF(z)^K=p/(1−F(z)), with denominator bounded away from zero. Coupling last observed reset with ultimate reset yields ||U^{-t}rho_tU^t−sigma||_1≤2P(L>t). Eigenbasis multiplication multiplies off-diagonal rho_ij by G(u_j/u_i), and triangle bounds on 1−F give the sharp nonzero floor. Two-stage r0=q,r1=(1−p−q)/(1−q),r_n=0 afterwards exhaust [p/(2−p),1] at z=−1. Nonzero G for all phases proves convergence iff commuting; Cesàro averaging removes gaps. For r_n=(n+2)^−2, telescoping p=1/2, f_k=1/[2k(k+1)], E[K²]=3 gives P(L>t)≤3/t. Independent finite recurrence and direct transform truncation checks corroborate, not replace, these all-time arguments.
residual_risks: Computational samples are finite and do not independently certify unquantified infinite-domain conditions.
